---
title: "Present full screen"
description: "Turn a notebook into slides and show it full screen, or share it as a file."
---

This guide covers marimo's slide view, presenting full screen and exporting
a deck to a single HTML file.

## Turn on the slide layout

marimo can lay out a notebook as slides: each cell output becomes a slide and
the code is hidden.

1. Open the notebook with `marimo edit deck.py`.
2. Open the app view (the preview button at the bottom right, or
   <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>.</kbd>).
3. In the layout menu of the app view, choose **Slides**.

marimo saves the choice in a `layouts/deck.slides.json` file and records it in
the notebook header:

```python
# fragment: the first lines of a notebook that uses the slide layout.
import marimo

app = marimo.App(width="full", layout_file="layouts/deck.slides.json")
```

`width="full"` lets the slides use the whole width of the window. Keep the
`layouts/` folder next to the notebook; without it, marimo shows the notebook
as a page.

## Present

Run the notebook as an app:

```bash
marimo run deck.py
```

marimo opens it in the browser with the slide layout. Press the
**Fullscreen** button at the bottom right of the slides: the slides fill the
screen and the arrow keys move between them (outside full screen, use the
arrows on the sides of the slide). Because banners draws every slide on a
16:9 canvas sized by the window width, the slides fill a projector without
changes.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Check the deck before the talk

Animations are rendered and cached the first time their cell runs. Running
the deck once before the talk means that, during the talk, every animation
comes from the cache and appears at once.
:::

## Share as a file

`marimo export html` runs the notebook and writes a single HTML file that
opens in any browser, without Python:

```bash
marimo export html deck.py -o deck.html
```

Slides, plots, tables, Mermaid diagrams and the click-through players of
`FlowAnimation` and `Manim` work in the exported file. `AnimatedGraph` does
not, because it needs the running notebook to answer the clicks.
